rationale: Same root as accumulated ⲣⲉϩⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'watcher' and ⲡⲓ̈ⲱⲣϩ 'the watcher,' but here functions in passive-object register: the visual impression looked at by the eyes and stored by the enthumesis. The sense-faculty as object (what-is-seen) rather than agent (one-who-sees).

Greek ἐνθύμησις applied here to the body's storing-faculty (rather than to the cosmic ⲡⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ 'counsel' of the five-faculty mapping). The body's enthumesis takes sense-impressions, stores them in inner storehouses (ⲛⲧⲁⲙⲟⲛ), and retrieves them on demand.
Compound: ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ϣⲱⲗⲙ̄ 'smell.' Standard Coptic formation parallel to ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲥ 'watch-post' in glossary. Designates the olfactory faculty as a place-of-functioning.

Compound: ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ϫⲓ ('take, receive') + ϯⲡⲉ ('taste,' already in glossary). The taste-faculty as a place-of-receiving-taste. Functions in parallel with ⲡⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙⲉ in the sense-enumeration.

Tentative — ⲡⲟⲁⲙⲟⲙ̄ unattested elsewhere; possibly Lyc. reduplicated verbal noun related to ⲱⲙ 'seize/swallow' or ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp,' here designating the touch-faculty (the fifth and final sense in the enumeration). ⲛⲟⲓⲝ = Lyc. plural of ϭⲓϫ 'hand.' Confidence low; flagged for parallels in subsequent kephalaia.

Lyc. compound of unclear analysis; possibly ⲟⲩⲣⲏ ('watch, guard') + ⲙ̄ϣⲉ ('of the post/wood') = 'watchmen at the post.' Context (men set upon gates with nets and guards) confirms a watching/gate-keeping function. Recurs lines 15 and 17. Tentative.

Crum 605b ϣⲁϣⲧ̄ 'snare, net.' Recurring throughout the parable (lines 16, 19, 20, 29, 31, 33) as the gate-stratagem of the watchmen — both screening device (catching strangers) and admission filter (released for citizens). Standard Coptic noun.

Lyc. plural of ⲣⲟ 'gate, mouth, door.' The gates of the city in the parable; allegorically the gates of the body (= the sense-organs through which impressions enter). Recurs throughout the parable section.
